papers.title: Retaining Naturally Fragmented Experience for Offline Reinforcement Learning: Evidence From Real Operational Logs
papers.summary: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) learns policies from fixed datasets, but real operational logs often contain missing or invalid measurements. Because offline RL requires multiple variables to be valid simultaneously, these imperfections can divide continuous records into disconnected fragments. This study preserves the naturally imperfect structure of real operational logs rather than reconstructing missing observations, which is a more faithful way to represent the recorded experience. papers.title: Robot Niko: A Life-Size 3D-Printed Humanoid Assistant on a Raspberry Pi - System Design and Build
papers.summary: Niko is a life-size humanoid assistant built in 2022 by Quanta Robotics, a student robotics team at Comilla University, at the FabLab of the Deputy Commissioner's Office in Cumilla, Bangladesh. Its body follows InMoov, the open-source 3D-printed humanoid: a head, torso, two arms and two five-fingered hands, on a stand over a wheeled base. Where InMoov is usually run by Arduino boards and the MyRobotLab framework, Niko runs from a single Raspberry Pi 4 with its own Python software. The primary outcome was electrode accuracy at the tip, 40 mm from the tip, and the entry point compared with the planned trajectory. papers.title: Physical AI Bridging the Digital Mind and the Material World
papers.summary: Physical AI is a pivotal moment in the interaction of machines with the physical world. It refers to a family of AI systems that interact with the physical world by integrating high-level models with sensors, actuators and control systems to perceive, reason, decide and act in the physical world. Physical AI, unlike generative or digital-only AI, that creates text, code or images within the confines of software, exists where what matters is measurable in motion, force and matter. papers.title: Understanding User Expectations Across Communication Modalities in Human-Robot Interaction: An Elicitation Study
papers.summary: Human-robot communication is essential to effective human-robot interaction. One way to improve this communication is to design systems that align with users’ mental models and expectations about how robots should convey information. However, little research has examined these expectations across robot morphologies (mobile robot, humanoid robot, manipulator, drone) and behaviors (“Navigation Intention,” “Operating State,” “Affect,” “Target Identification,” “Interaction Intention”). This work addresses that gap through an elicitation study investigating users’ expected communication modalities

papers.title: Robotic-assisted knee arthroplasty methods provide insight into Homo neanderthalensis gait and the evolutionary origins of modern human knee variation
papers.summary: Abstract Lower-limb alignment is central to human bipedal locomotion and a key determinant of joint kinematics and osteoarthritis risk in modern clinical practice. However, its significance in hominins, and therefore its evolutionary implications, remain poorly understood. Advances in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) provide highly precise measurements of lower-limb alignment, joint morphology and soft-tissue balance that can elucidate these understudied aspects of hominin functional morphology. papers.title: Adaptive Maintenance in Intelligent Production Systems via the Synergistic Integration of Digital Twin and Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: The growing complexity of production systems demands intelligent maintenance strategies to enhance efficiency and reliability. This study proposes a Reinforcement Learning (RL)–based maintenance decision framework integrated within a digital twin environment for data-driven production management. The proposed approach combines real-time system state monitoring, digital twins, and RL to learn adaptive maintenance policies. papers.title: Replication Data for: Decentralized Reinforcement Learning-Based MAC Optimization for Dense LoRa Networks
papers.summary: This dataset contains simulation code, experiment configurations, recorded results and analysis scripts supporting the MSc dissertation “Decentralized Reinforcement Learning-Based MAC Optimization for Dense LoRa Networks” by Xiangyu Zou. The experiments compare tabular Q-learning, individual-reward DQN and shared-reward DQN with ALOHA and TDMA under varying node densities and traffic loads. The accompanying documentation identifies the files and commands used to reproduce the principal figures and tables.

papers.title: Robust design of air chamber to enhance impact connection strength of magnetic connectors on modular truss robots
papers.summary: The connection mechanisms between neighboring modules are crucial subsystems in modular reconfigurable robot (MRR) systems. Magnetic connectors have been widely used for docking and undocking because of their mechanical simplicity and ease of use. However, they suffer from lower maximum tensile strength compared with mechanical docking mechanisms. This limitation is critical when modular truss robots are subjected to impact forces during locomotion, reconfiguration, docking, and undocking. papers.summary: How many platforms compete for each kind of AI training work, and how much of it does the leader hold?
